methodology.description: Pass 1 streams CSV records and writes only a 128-bit candidate fingerprint, file ID, and byte offset to a temporary SQLite index. Pass 2 considers only fingerprints occurring more than once, rereads those source records, and compares full canonical feature rows using disk-backed representative locators. No full feature row is persisted in the scratch database.
methodology.record_offsets: Offsets are captured from a binary stream immediately before csv.reader parses each logical record. Its lazy physical-line iterator preserves quoted fields, escaped quotes, CRLF and quoted multiline records. Candidate rereads seek to the captured byte offset and parse one complete logical CSV record.
methodology.canonicalization: Each of the 39 fields is parsed as a numeric float64 and encoded little-endian. Signed zero is normalized to positive zero and NaNs to the platform's canonical Python NaN encoding; infinities retain sign. Folder labels use the existing multiclass mapping, including Benign_Final to Benign.
methodology.collision_safety: BLAKE2b-128 is only a candidate fingerprint. Every candidate is reread and its complete 312-byte canonical row is compared against representative source rows. A fingerprint collision with different features creates separate representatives and is not counted as a duplicate.
methodology.duplicate_definitions: Complete-row identity is the canonical 39-feature row plus folder-derived label. Feature-only representatives separately identify conflicting-label groups. Duplicate occurrences are records beyond the first for a feature/label group; within-file excess and additional represented files are reported separately.
methodology.fingerprint: BLAKE2b 128-bit candidate only; full 39-feature verification required
methodology.scratch_estimate: 128 bytes per source row plus 20% headroom; this is a planning estimate, while the 8 GiB audit-owned file cap is enforced during execution.

limitations: Labels are provenance labels derived from category folders, not independent ground truth.
The audit counts duplicates and never removes or changes source records.
No capture/session independence is inferred from file boundaries.
The 128-byte-per-row scratch estimate is a planning estimate, not a measured database size; the 8 GiB cap and 2 GiB free-space reserve are enforced during the run.

A pathological fingerprint bucket containing many distinct rows can make exact representative comparisons slow; disk use remains capped and the audit stops incomplete if its cap or free-space reserve is threatened.
